A.reason: All candidates respect the resource and privacy constraints and check availability, condition, cleanup effort and seated access. Distinct primary mechanisms are centralized return handling, visible category destinations, an on-site reserve, optional shared tidying, reader condition screening and physical stack stability. Candidate 5 repairs candidate 0's overload handling rather than introducing a new mechanism. It is strongest because it bounds volunteer work, specifies full-box behavior and provides observable backlog and fallback criteria, while acknowledging weaker screening during direct returns.

B.reason: All candidates are usable without definite serious hard-constraint violations. Their primary mechanisms are centralized return handling, visible category destinations, an on-site reserve, optional shared tidying and portable return reminders. Candidate 0 offers the clearest low-decision borrowing ritual and predictable volunteer routine, with checks covering all required outcomes. Its main weakness is detecting return-box overload without specifying an operational fallback.

pair.reason: A5 improves the otherwise comparable B0 ritual by specifying how readers and volunteers respond to a full box or unfinished inspection within the fixed visits. Its explicit fallback and stopping criteria make the pilot more feasible and inspectable. The added instructions introduce some complexity, but address a concrete capacity failure.
